turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, give me a second, this thing's after freezing again. Right. What has you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah it's nothing. I wouldn't be here only she dragged me down. And the parking out there is a disgrace, we were circling twenty minutes.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Don't mind her. She found a lump in the shower and she's been pretending it isn't there.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): It's a small lump, left breast. I felt it washing. No pain in it. Sure it's probably just a cyst.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the screen jumped on me. Left side, did you say? Say it again.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Left breast. Little lump. Painless. Size of a pea, maybe a bit over. I noticed it in the shower.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): When was that?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm. Last week, I think. Or the week before. I don't be checking myself. I can't put a date on it.
[SEG0009] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She told me about it last week anyway. She still wouldn't ring ye.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any stuff coming from the nipple? Blood, milk, clear fluid?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing out of the nipple. It's grand.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sore at all, or tender when you press it?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No pain. Not even when I press it. I told you it's not a bother.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the other breast, or under the arm, any other lumps?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Just that one. I had a feel. Nothing else.
[SEG0016] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Our mother had breast cancer. She was only fifty-five. Siobhan's forty-six now, you should say that.
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah she did. She was fifty-five. She's years out the other side of it. Doesn't mean I've it.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fifty-five, was it? Sorry, say that again, I'm half on this referral screen.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Fifty-five. Mother. Breast cancer. That's the whole of it.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any weight dropping off, night sweats, or are you wrecked tired?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Weight's the same. No sweats. Energy's fine. I'm well able.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tablets. What are you taking? The list on here looks ancient.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Only the water tablet. Little white one, for the blood pressure and the ankles. And Nurofen the odd time if I've a headache.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): The water tablet, which one? Dose? Say it again, I've lost the cursor.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Bendrofluzide. Two point five milligrams. Once in the morning. A year or more now.
[SEG0026] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She has the purple inhaler as well. She leaves it in the drawer and pretends she doesn't.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah I hardly touch it. I don't even know the name of it. Purple thing for if I get wheezy rushing about. I'm not asthmatic.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Purple inhaler. What's printed on it? I need the name.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): I haven't a notion. It's just purple. I use it the odd time. Hardly worth writing down.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Hop up on the bed there. One second, this alert won't clear.

[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ok. Small firm lump, left breast, upper outer part, about a centimetre and a half, moves under the fingers. Skin over it is normal, no dimpling. Nipple isn't pulled in. Nothing in the armpit and the right breast feels clear.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): See? Tiny. I said ye'd find nothing worth worrying about.
[SEG0033] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It's still a lump, Siobhan. Let him talk.

[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm not calling it nothing. Feeling it, I can't tell a cyst from something we'd need to rule out. With your mother having it at fifty-five, it goes to the breast clinic urgent.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Urgent? For a pea? That's a bit much.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's the pathway. I'll send the referral today. They see the urgent ones inside 2 weeks.
[SEG0037] person_3 (CAREGIVER): And what about tests here?

[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): The nurse takes bloods Thursday morning, eight o'clock. Kidney function and a full blood count, because of the water tablet. Take the tablet after the bloods, not before. No need to fast.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday? I'm working Thursday. Sure can it not wait till after the weekend?
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thursday morning is the slot that's booked. Eight o'clock, in and out. If those bloods are borderline we'll do a third test, the liver profile. Not booking that now.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the wheeze. If it does not settle, a scan, just a chest x-ray. Only if it doesn't settle.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): It always settles. I don't need an x-ray.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's fine. It's only if. And I'll see you back here in two weeks, with the clinic and the bloods. Reception will book it on the way out.
[SEG0044] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll make sure she goes. She'll try to cancel, you watch.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): I won't cancel. I just think ye're all going overboard. It's a little lump.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back sooner if the skin changes or it gets bigger before then. Otherwise two weeks, and Thursday for the bloods. Mind yourselves.

spec.situation: Woman in her forties who found a painless lump in the left breast in the shower; no nipple discharge; mother had breast cancer at fifty-five; examination described; urgent clinic referral.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Conditional chest x-ray is supported; indication 'wheeze does not settle' is implied, not explicitly stated as wheeze.
bad.text: Chest x-ray (type=imaging, status=conditional, requested_by=doctor, indication=if the wheeze does not settle)

omissions.text: Breast lump described by patient as about the size of a pea, maybe a bit over.
No nipple discharge specifically included no blood, milk, or clear fluid.
Examination found the skin over the left breast lump was normal.
Doctor planned to send the urgent breast clinic referral today.
